title: Redis session store product, tier, placement, availability target, session lifetime, eviction, capacity, persistence and RPO/RTO are not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 4 (shared platform: gateway-bff + Redis session), 8 (gateway-bff, Redis session, Key Vault), 27 (Spring Cloud Gateway, session in Redis), 33 (browser session cookie, opaque, 15 min idle; gateway-bff OUT: DB Redis sessions only, no business data), 35 (sign-in at the shared gateway-bff, Entra ID, MFA, 15-minute idle timeout); Program BRD v4 section 6.1 NFR-002, section 6.4 NFR-020, NFR-021, NFR-022, NFR-023
section: Preconditions; Authority; Data; Solution plan settings; Traceability
description: The architecture places a Redis session store next to gateway-bff as shared platform, states that it holds sessions only and no business data, and fixes the 15-minute idle timeout of the browser session. It does not state the product (Azure Cache for Redis or the bank's shared Redis service), the tier and the memory, the zone and region placement, the availability target that applies to the store itself, the absolute session lifetime beyond the idle timeout, the eviction policy, the maximum number of concurrent sessions the store must carry, the persistence and backup choice, or the recovery point and recovery time objectives for the store. The story can provision and test the store, but it cannot fix these values without an infrastructure decision.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 4: shared platform (not in the 19) lists gateway-bff + Redis session; slide 8: gateway-bff, Redis session, Key Vault; slide 27: Spring Cloud Gateway, Redis session; slide 33: REST Browser /api/recovery/** via App Gateway, session cookie (opaque, 15 min idle) and DB Redis: sessions only; no business data; slide 35: ACE Common sign-in (Entra ID, MFA) at the shared gateway-bff, 15-minute idle timeout; slide 48: RPO/RTO not yet set; Program BRD v4 NFR-022 and NFR-023 Open, following the ACE objectives; NFR-002 about 370 staff online in the busiest hour of 914 named users
proposed: Fix the product, the tier and memory, the zone and region placement, the availability target, the absolute session lifetime, the eviction policy, the maximum concurrent sessions, the persistence and backup choice and the RPO/RTO for the session store at the platform infrastructure review before wave 0 exit, and record them in the Service Catalog and the platform runbook.

title: gateway-bff public path table, inbox push transport and payment-tab operation are not stated by any source
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Ownership Map v1
description: No source gives the gateway-bff OpenAPI or AsyncAPI document, the public path of the four screen tabs, the inbox stream path, the transport of the inbox push, or which rwb-payment operation serves a case-scoped payments tab. Architecture v5 gives only /api/recovery/** and /api/recovery/cases/{id}, and slide 10 names the tab owners without paths; the Ownership Map names GET /cases/{caseId}/documents (P5), GET /notices/{noticeId} (P6), GET /proceeds (P8) and GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId} (S4).
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 8 (App Gateway routes /recovery/* and /api/recovery/* to gateway-bff); slide 10 (browser calls /api/recovery/cases/{id}; Documents rwb-document, Notices rwb-comms, Payments rwb-payment, Legal rwb-litigation); slide 20 (REST browser /api/recovery/** via App Gateway with an opaque session cookie, 15 min idle; EVT ApprovalRequested and TimerBreached to the officer inbox push)
proposed: Publish the route document at the edge contract review, with one path per screen tab and one inbox stream path, and confirm the payment-tab and notice-tab operations with rwb-payment and rwb-comms at the same review.

title: gateway-bff deployment topology, screen-model schema, inbox push transport and gateway sizing are not stated by any source
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Ownership Map v1
description: No source states the deployment topology of the gateway (pods per environment, resource limits, connection pools), the field list and shape of the screen model it assembles, the transport of the officer inbox push, or the memory and connection sizing of the gateway and its Redis session store. Architecture v5 fixes the call behaviour, the 2 s timeout, the breaker per downstream, the 15-minute idle and the 0.15 + 0.6 + 0.3 s budget, and nothing about the runtime unit.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 8 (gateway-bff, Spring Cloud Gateway, session in Redis); slide 10 (composition into the screen model, response budget, timeouts, breaker per downstream, GET retried once with jitter); slide 20 (session cookie, 15 min idle, owner service one hop in parallel, Redis sessions only, no business data); no slide gives a pod count, a model field list or a push transport
proposed: Fix the topology and the screen-model field list in the edge design review with the platform team and RWB-PLT-N006-INF, and record the push transport with the ACE front-end team before the first integration test.

title: DMZ network design, gateway product, FAPI 2.0 settings, external identity provider, certificate lifecycle, rate limits, WAF rule set and DR target of the partner gateway are not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 7 (system context: partner gateway, FAPI 2.0 to S9), 8 and 8 notes (partners use the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) that fronts rwb-partner), 17 (rwb-partner IN: Partner portal /partner/v1/* (FAPI 2.0); Partners (law firms, agencies, buyers): via partner gateway, MFA), 20 (partners do not use gateway-bff), 35 and 35 notes (shared App Gateway with WAF; partners only through the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0); FAPI 2.0 Security Profile final Feb 2025: sender-constrained tokens, PAR, strong client authentication, separate DMZ gateway, penetration test before launch; NIST SP 800-204 and OWASP API Top 10); Program BRD v4 REQ-ACA-012, REQ-S9-008, NFR-003, NFR-056, NFR-063; Epic 2 BRD v2 RWB-E2-019
section: Preconditions; Exception paths; State transitions; Data; Contract 12.2; Solution plan; Out of scope
description: The architecture fixes the partner gateway's existence, its role as the only partner entry point fronting rwb-partner, the FAPI 2.0 profile with pushed authorisation requests, sender-constrained tokens and strong client authentication, a separate DMZ gateway and a penetration test before launch, and it fixes multi-factor sign-in and roles per partner. It does not state the DMZ network design (zones, subnets, address plan, firewall pair, ingress and egress rules), the gateway product and its version, the client authentication method for a confidential client (mTLS alone or private_key_jwt), the access and refresh token lifetimes, the external identity provider that federates a partner user and its protocol, the certificate validity, the overlap window and the revocation propagation time, the rate-limit values and the request size limit, the WAF rule set, or the recovery point and recovery time objectives of the DMZ gateway. The story can provision, configure and test the edge, but it cannot fix these values without a security and infrastructure decision.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 7: partner gateway in the system context, FAPI 2.0 to S9, /recovery/* via App Gateway for staff; slide 8: Partner gateway FAPI 2.0 to S9, edge notes, partners use the partner gateway that fronts rwb-partner; slide 17: rwb-partner IN REST Staff GET/POST /partners, /instructions and Partner portal /partner/v1/* (FAPI 2.0), OUT note Partners via partner gateway, MFA; slide 20: gateway-bff IN REST Browser /api/recovery/** via App Gateway, session cookie, and REST Partners do not use it: partner gateway to rwb-partner; slide 35: Edge shared App Gateway with WAF, partners only through the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0); notes: Partners: FAPI 2.0 Security Profile (final Feb 2025) for the partner API - sender-constrained tokens, PAR, strong client authentication; separate DMZ gateway; penetration test before launch; zero trust per NIST SP 800-204 and OWASP API Top 10 including object-level authorisation; Program BRD v4 NFR-003 about 50 partner users online of about 320 named, NFR-056 penetration test and security review before the first production release and before the partner portal opens to users outside the bank, NFR-063 desktop browsers and tablets
proposed: Fix the DMZ zone design and its firewall policy, the gateway product and version, the client authentication method, the access and refresh token lifetimes, the external identity provider and its protocol, the certificate validity, the overlap window and the revocation propagation time, the rate-limit values, the request size limit, the WAF rule set and the DR objectives in the security design authority review before the penetration test, and record them in the security design decision, the Service Catalog and the gateway runbook.

title: Airflow product, tenancy, DAG names, identity method, timeout and retry values, the DailyCaseRun wait contract and the file-window operation are not stated
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 5, 8, 9, 11, 15, 16 and 20; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 sections 6.3 and 6.4
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 9 State transitions; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.6 Schedules; 13 Solution plan
description: Architecture v5 fixes the placement of the bank's Airflow (outside the AKS cluster, replacing Control-M, for discussion) and its five duties, and it fixes the REST contract the chain calls. It states no product, version or tenancy, no DAG names, no identity method for the scheduler (service principal, certificate or another mechanism), no timeout and retry values, no statement of how the DAG waits for DailyCaseRun (poll or callback) and no operation for the WIN and debt-buyer file windows; Architecture v5 slides 16 and 20 name the activity and the window, not a path. The Ownership Map has a row for GET /data-products/freshness (P1) and no row for the business-date-ready call, the extract-run call or the file-window call, so those paths cannot be confirmed from the map either. The edge cannot be built, tested and handed over without these values, and the file-window payload overlaps the gap already open on RWB-E1-007.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 5 note (the bank moves from Control-M to Airflow, for discussion; the chain runs cross-system overnight, fixed-window file transfers, report extracts and one-off bulk loads, and calls services through their APIs, never their schemas); slide 9 note (the five duties: ACE ingestion DAG, business date ready then wait for DailyCaseRun, WIN and debt-buyer windows, report extracts in rwb-reporting, cutover loads and backfills; APIs only, never rwb_* schemas); slide 11 (REST: user JWT from the BFF plus workload identity, 2 s timeout, GET retried once, Idempotency-Key on every POST, RFC 9457); slide 15 (rwb-source-data IN: POST /business-days/{date}/ready (Airflow) and GET /freshness); slide 16 (rwb-integration: Airflow window WIN file 16:00, buyer files per lot); slide 20 (rwb-reporting IN: POST /reports/{id}/run (Airflow)); Ownership Map v1 rows for GET /data-products/freshness (P1), GET /reports/measures (P9) and GET /admin/outbound-items (P2), and no row for the three calls above.
proposed: Fix the Airflow product, tenancy, service principal, timeout and retry values, the DailyCaseRun wait mechanism and the three owner operation paths and payloads at the scheduling design review with the bank's scheduling team, the ACE platform team and the owners of rwb-source-data, rwb-integration and rwb-reporting, and publish them in the owner CON stories before the first SIT chain run.
